name: Question 9
problem:
$$
f(\theta ,ϕ)=⟨5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\text{_____}⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(\theta ,ϕ)$ above parametrizes the ellipsoid defined in Cartesian coordinates as $\frac{{x}^{2}}{25}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}+{z}^{2}=1.$ What is the third component of $f?$
worked_solution:
First, we make the following substitution:

$$
x=5X,\,y=2Y,\,z=Z
$$

Substituting the above into the Cartesian equation of our ellipsoid, we get

$$
{X}^{2}+{Y}^{2}+{Z}^{2}=1,
$$

which is the equation of a sphere of radius $1$ centered at the origin in $(X,Y,Z)$ coordinates.
In spherical polar coordinates, this sphere has the equation $\rho =1.$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical polar coordinates of a point, then its $(X,Y,Z)$ coordinates can be found using the following formulas:

$$
X=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,Y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,Z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨5X,2Y,Z⟩ \\  & =⟨5\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,2\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨5\cdot 1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,2\cdot 1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ and $ϕ\in [-\pi ,\pi ].$

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.$

Question 9
?

f(θ,ϕ)=⟨5cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,2sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,_____⟩

The vector-valued function f(θ,ϕ) above parametrizes the ellipsoid defined in Cartesian coordinates as x225+y24+z2=1. What is the third component of f?

a
2sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ
b
cos⁡ϕ
c
2sin⁡θcos⁡ϕ
d
sin⁡ϕcos⁡ϕ
e
5cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we make the following substitution:

x=5X,y=2Y,z=Z

Substituting the above into the Cartesian equation of our ellipsoid, we get

X2+Y2+Z2=1,

which is the equation of a sphere of radius 1 centered at the origin in (X,Y,Z) coordinates. In spherical polar coordinates, this sphere has the equation ρ=1.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical polar coordinates of a point, then its (X,Y,Z) coordinates can be found using the following formulas: X=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,Y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,Z=ρcos⁡ϕ.

Now, for any point (x,y,z) on our surface, we obtain the following:

f(θ,ϕ)=⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨5X,2Y,Z⟩=⟨5ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,2ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ⟩=⟨5⋅1⋅cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,2⋅1⋅sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,1⋅cos⁡ϕ⟩=⟨5cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,2sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,cos⁡ϕ⟩

where θ∈[0,2π) and ϕ∈[−π,π].

Therefore, the third component of f is cos⁡ϕ.
